name: llama-cpp-kleidiai
description: llama.cpp's Arm KleidiAI SME2/SVE2 matmul kernels (kai_run_matmul_*) -- the target this whole project was built around.
why_it_matters: llama.cpp's own startup banner prints 'KLEIDIAI = 1' and 'kleidiai: primary q4 kernel feature SME2' at model load, but neither line proves the SME2 kernel ever executes a single matmul. This is the project's headline finding: an official release build compiles ZERO kai_run_matmul symbols while still being able to print this banner if built differently, and even a from-source build with KleidiAI genuinely compiled in silently collapses to NEON for decode above the chip's SME thread cap. See results/GROUND-TRUTH-DISPATCH.md and the upstream issue ggml-org/llama.cpp#26547.

l1.note: Same regex and family order tools/verify_dispatch.py has always used (DEFAULT_DISPATCH_REGEX / _FAMILY_ORDER) -- this preset is asserted to reproduce that tool's L1 result exactly, not just approximate it.

patterns.label: buffer_type_fallback
patterns.regex: cannot be used with preferred buffer type (\S+)

patterns.label: no_kernel_warning
patterns.regex: kleidiai: no kernel for tensor type (\S+), not accelerated

l2.note: 'advertised_family' mirrors verify_dispatch.py's run_l2_select()/compute_verdict() exactly: the q4 primary_kernel_feature line is what 'advertised' means for this target, because the models this project measured are all Q4_0/Q8_0.

l3.note: Regex breakpoint (lldb) or per-symbol pending breakpoints (gdb), auto-continuing, non-halting -- see tools/dispatch_probe.lldb / tools/dispatch_probe.gdb. Anchored at the symbol start on purpose: an unanchored pattern also matches the compiler-generated template thunk and double-counts (see dispatch_probe.lldb's header).

workload.note: Same flag shape run_l2_select()/run_l3_lldb()/run_l3_gdb() have always built. threads=2 by default because the M4 Max's sme_thread_cap is 2 (see results/GROUND-TRUTH-DISPATCH.md) -- at this thread count the plain SME2 path fires on the short default prompt; sweep --param threads=8 to reproduce the silent-fallback finding.

verified_against.result: `polygraph check llama-cpp-kleidiai --binary .../llama-cli --model q05.gguf --param threads=2` and `verify_dispatch.py --binary ... --model ... --threads 2 --workloads decode_short` produced the SAME verdict (SME2_DISPATCHED) and a BYTE-IDENTICAL l3.hits_by_symbol dict (17 kai_run_matmul_* symbols, 3 non-zero, summing to 5826 hits both ways; L1 found 17/264 kai_-prefixed symbols matching ^kai_run_matmul). Compared programmatically, not by eye.

verified_against.platform: darwin-arm64 (Apple M4 Max), scanning a linux/aarch64 artifact
verified_against.artifact: official llama.cpp b10276 ubuntu-arm64 release tarball (/tmp/llamacpp_investigation), and the official macos-arm64 release tarball
verified_against.result: L1 correctly reports 0/0 kai_run_matmul symbols on BOTH official release artifacts (KleidiAI is off by default in releases) -- confirms the project's headline finding independent of this repo's own from-source build, and confirms this preset fails closed (not silently 0) rather than guessing.

caveats: L2's 'advertised_family' is read from the q4 primary-kernel-feature line specifically; a model quantized as something other than Q4_0/Q8_0 will show primary_kernel_feature keyed under a different tensor type and 'advertised' will read as null (verdict becomes *_EXECUTED_NO_ADVERTISED_FEATURE, not a false MISMATCH).
